body:
Phase 3 (closing audit) of design #4592 — *a verified cursor covers only a restorable chain: replication admission, finished* (pkgs/id). Design doc: `files/designs/code-id-replication-admission.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

**Gated on Phases 1–2 of #4592 landing** (Phase 1 = #4471, the restore range at the envelope; Phase 2 = #4487, snapshot monotonicity). Do not start the audit before both land.

## Scope

Land the contract statement in the `ReplicationTracker` module doc (`pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs`) and produce the closing admission inventory: every precondition `WorldCore::restore` demands of a journal, dispositioned against a check in `ReplicationTracker::accept` — *holds at accept* / *holds at restore only, with the reason that is safe* / *gap, filed as a named follow-up issue*. The inventory is the deliverable; fixing a confirmed gap inside this issue is out of scope beyond a single-site slip (file it instead).

## Required dispositions

- **(a) Entry-kind version gating** — a payload whose header version is in-range but whose entries include a kind that requires a higher header version (`header_version_for_entry`, `world/mod.rs`): can a signed in-range snapshot carry e.g. an `ExecutionProfile` entry on a v1 header, and does restore's application of it produce a state a real v1 journal could never hold? Disposition with evidence either way.
- **(b) Session-bootstrap version source** — where `ReplicationTracker::new`'s `header_version` argument comes from in the serve wiring, whether #4592's decision 2 (an out-of-range session version makes the tracker inert under the accept-side range check) holds at that call site, and whether a *new* session may legitimately start below the version a previous session reached (monotonicity is per-tracker; answer from the bootstrap code, not assumption).
- **(c) Pre-fix terminal hygiene** — Terminal frames carrying an out-of-range version against a tracker whose version was set by a pre-Phase-1 snapshot: expected to be covered by Phase 1's all-kinds range check — confirm with a test or a code citation, don't assume.
- **(d) Second doors** — any caller of `accept` (or of the frame decode path) that pre-validates header versions itself: disposition each as removed, delegated to `accept`, or named exception with the reason.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The contract statement from #4592 ("a frame is admitted only if its header version names a chain that could exist…") is present in the `replication.rs` module doc, cross-referenced from the `accept` doc comment.
- [ ] The inventory is posted on this issue: one row per restore precondition (header presence/shape, header world, header version range, per-entry decodability, payload header agreement — the landed #4486 leg — plus anything the audit finds), each with its disposition and evidence (file:line or test name).
- [ ] Required dispositions (a)–(d) are each answered on this issue with evidence.
- [ ] Any confirmed gap is filed as a named follow-up issue and linked here — not fixed inside the audit beyond a single-site slip.
- [ ] Evidence is posted on #4592 (and on feature epic #806 if its phase tracking names the admission contract) summarising the inventory outcome.
- [ ] `cargo test -p id --lib world::replication` passes (CI or laptop per repo rules — no builds on the sandbox).

## Related

Design #4592; phases #4471 (Phase 1), #4487 (Phase 2); landed sibling leg #4486; feature epic #806.
